A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DECO-G research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original GSM8k, ACE05, and SummEval experiments, alongside pruning, entropy, and generation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds broader Ctrl-G comparisons and measured inference latency.

M1.justification: Both versions use instruction-aware HMM distillation, pivot/wildcard trie construction, FEM probability reweighting, and top-k state pruning. V2 expands the trie formalization and explicitly describes normalization, without establishing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Natural-Instructions-v2 distillation and evaluation on GSM8k, ACE05-EN, and SummEval remain unchanged. The added latency experiment uses existing GSM8k coverage rather than a new task or scenario.

E2.justification: V1 includes only a limited Ctrl-G GSM8k result and example in Appendix C. V2 includes Ctrl-G across all three models in Tables 1–3, the full ACE05 results, and the entropy and latency comparisons. NL/JSON and their structured variants are retained under clearer Prompt-Only/Outlines names.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a GSM8k timing evaluation reporting milliseconds per token and relative latency on one NVIDIA A100. Existing zero-shot greedy evaluation, model configurations, task metrics, and prompt templates remain unchanged; omitted training settings represent lost documentation rather than an established protocol change.

E4.justification: New Table 5 measures pruning's latency effect and compares decoding overhead. V1 already contained pruning accuracy, hidden-state mass retention, FLOP calculations, entropy analysis, and the Ctrl-G failure example; these are retained and substantially relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The entropy analysis retains its 100-example sample, and the figures do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive Ctrl-G scores, entropy bars, and latency results, including 5.12 ms/token for DECO-G versus 3.07 for Prompt-Only and 9.45 without pruning. Existing DECO-G benchmark scores remain unchanged. The Ctrl-G GSM8k passage changes from 60.6% to 61.6%, now explicitly identifying Llama. Table 2 corrects Qwen3 JSON AI+ from 3.01 to 30.1, matching v1's appendix. New entropy bars place Ctrl-G below DECO-G for Llama and Qwen3.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a formal state-convergence condition in Equation 3, a minimal-DFA claim, and an exponential-versus-linear complexity argument, O(K^N) versus O(NK). V1 defined pivots and wildcards but described compact construction qualitatively. Existing Bayesian/HMM recurrences and pruning-cost derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list replace the explicit 1.0%–6.0% relative-gain claim with unquantified consistent improvements over prompting and structured generation. The central decoupling contribution, three technical components, and format-compliance guarantee remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5.1 explains claimed scalability advantages for constraints at arbitrary positions and chained wildcard templates, and characterizes measured latency overhead as minimal. Some qualifications, including Llama's SummEval weaknesses, disappear from the discussion. The existing limitations are retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: V2 announces code release and supplies a repository link, replacing v1's conditional code-and-weights release promise. It adds normalization detail but removes the 100 HMM training epochs, 56/1 GPU-hour sampling/training costs, Qwen's 152k vocabulary specification, and explicit ACE05 metric-matching criteria. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Loula et al. (2025) on sequential Monte Carlo and Lipkin et al. (2025) on weighted rejection sampling. It elaborates scalability positioning against Ctrl-G and structured generation while retaining the same GeLaTo/Ctrl-G lineage and principal novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, trie explanation, and related work undergo substantial rewriting. ACE05 and SummEval sections swap order; efficiency analysis moves into the main text, entropy discussion and reproducibility move to appendices, and limitations move out of the appendix.

P2.justification: V2 changes from a single-column conference layout to two columns, redesigns table grouping, simplifies Figure 2, and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It adds the latency table and redraws the entropy figure with Ctrl-G bars and revised labels and axes. Existing pruning displays move into the main text.

improvement.justification: Broader Ctrl-G comparisons and measured latency materially strengthen empirical assessment. However, v2 removes reproducibility details and retains the lowest-entropy interpretation despite contrary new bars in Figure 4. Its new Equation 3 also leaves unresolved how merging all wildcard realizations preserves their length bounds, weakening the claimed complexity guarantee. These empirical gains coexist with material documentation losses and unresolved argument validity, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
